title: Rule ID validation allows conflicting sessions
description:
File: rust/lichen-schc/src/fragment.rs
Lines: 847-853, 920-926

Issue: The receiver accepts fragments from any rule ID on first contact, then locks to that rule ID. This creates a race condition where an attacker can send a fragment with rule_id=X before the legitimate sender, causing legitimate fragments with rule_id=Y to be rejected (abort).

Trigger: On a shared channel, an attacker can race to claim the receiver state with any rule_id, causing legitimate fragmented transfers to fail.

Mitigation: Pre-configure expected rule_id at receiver construction, or document that callers must filter frames by rule_id before calling receive.
close_reason: Already implemented: AuthenticatedFragmentReceiver validates rule_id BEFORE calling inner receiver. Lines 2826 and 2853 check `payload.first() != Some(self.rule_id)` rejecting mismatched rule_ids with InvalidPeerEvidence. The inner FragmentReceiver's 'accept any rule_id on first contact' behavior is only exposed via test-only raw-fragment-codec feature. Test coverage in adaptation_vectors.rs:362-391 confirms wrong-direction rule_ids are rejected without state mutation.
